I had no retrieved literature, so these hypotheses rest on known NAS-Bench-201 regularities:

- Gains from convolutions saturate when other paths into the output are already strong.
- Replacing `none` gives the largest gain.
- Removing an edge hurts more when it is the main remaining path.
- Edits downstream of a dead node have no effect.

I have not checked any of them against benchmark data.
